messages:
Asha: heads up — Acme on mobile reports a 401 for /v1/generate but they say there’s no trace/request token in their payload. Can we get a tiny checklist I can send to the customer?

Leo: short checklist: ask for (1) the session snapshot/debug token from Console, (2) a minimal curl showing headers, (3) a HAR or SDK log excerpt, and (4) a screenshot of the request row in Console if token not visible. Mention proxies can strip headers.

Asha: can you paste an explicit curl example and the exact Console path? customer is behind an outbound proxy.

Tim: Console path: Console -> Requests (left nav) -> set time range to the incident window -> find the request row -> click it -> open "Session snapshot" panel -> click "Copy debug token". If that button is absent, tell them to screenshot the request row and role/permissions.

DevX: minimal curl to ask for (tell them to replace <KEY> and <URL> with theirs):
```
curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"test"}'
```
Ask them to include the full curl stdout (the -v output) so we can see response headers. If they can, also run with `-D -` to capture response headers but -v is fine.

Leo: header names to call out in your ask: we commonly look for x-rw-session (client side session header), x-rw-trace (service trace header), and the Authorization header. Add a note: "If you use a proxy, check proxy logs for x-rw-session / x-rw-trace — proxies sometimes remove custom headers."

DevX: browser HAR steps: DevTools -> Network -> reproduce -> right click any request -> Save all as HAR with content. Tell them to trim to the single failing request if possible. For mobile: ask for adb logcat (Android) or device console logs (iOS) with a ~1 minute window around the failure and grep for "RequestSnapshot" or "x-rw-session" strings.

SupportBot: Quick troubleshooting hints: (a) 401 with no trace token often = rotated API key or malformed Authorization header. (b) If the Console shows a request but no debug token, it could be obfuscated by a gateway — get HAR or proxy logs.

Tim: template to paste to customer (short):
"Could you: 1) Copy the Session Snapshot from Console (Console -> Requests -> find timestamp -> Session snapshot -> Copy debug token), 2) Run a minimal curl against the same endpoint with `-v` and paste the output, 3) If using browser, attach a HAR for the failing request, 4) If mobile, attach the device logs (look for x-rw-session or RequestSnapshot). If you can’t locate the snapshot button, please send a screenshot of the request row and your Console role name."

Asha: perfect. I’ll send that now. Thanks all :pray:

Leo: one more — ask them to include the exact timestamp (UTC) of an example request and the region they call (e.g., us-west-2). Helps us find the server-side trace fast.

Asha: noted and included. will escalate if they attach everything. :thumbsup:
